messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A job laid out across an entire bench. a small screw head strips at the last moment. You are tired of repeating the same approach. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "i stop moving and tap the screw head with my thumbnail. “it clicks once,” i say, tracing the old groove with my fingers. i leave the bench unfinished and the screw stuck in the corner. i put a folded receipt beside it and keep the old approach close by."}, {"id": "R026", "response": "the screw taps my thigh. i press the head hard. the screw slides. i press the bench with my palm. the screw stays. i turn and pull the screw under the bench. the bench stays. the screw taps my leg. i press the screw with my palm. the bench stays."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "i put the screw head under the bench and leave the bench open. the screw stays beneath the dust. i put my hand near the last strip and mark it with a pencil. the job can wait."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "1. stop. 2. check the head. 3. check the watch. slow. 4. check the tinkered corner. 5. check the dust. 6. check the bench. 7. i keep it tidy. 8. ask the watch for the square. 9. i mark the place."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "i reach for the screwdriver again, but i stop and photograph the screw head. i pull it back, then put it back. sorry—sorry, i’m checking the bench before i repeat the mistake."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "i tap the screw head with my knuckle, then leave it there for one second. i lean closer and keep my fingers on the bench. if the screw still catches, i mark the spot with pencil and leave the screw alone."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "i stop. the screw head drops into my palm. i rub my greasy fingertips together. “not the same,” i say. i move the screw head closer to the bench, then tap the bench with a rusted bolt. “useful soon.”"}, {"id": "R032", "response": "I tap the screw head once and leave it there. I turn the bench once and tap the bench again. I tap the screw head once more."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "I keep the screw head and tap the bench with the heel of my hand. I push the head back and count three steps before tapping again. I leave the screw head seated and rub the last three steps with a folded cloth."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "I rub the screw head once and set it down. I rub the bench once more, then try the next attempt with the head still loose. If the head still catches, I leave it alone and move it closer to the bench."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "i hold the screw head down and my grip tight. “i did not,” i say. “i did not. i did not. i did not. i do not know why i did not.” i move the bench two centimeters closer, then stop. “i do not know why i did not.”"}, {"id": "R036", "response": "i put the screw head in my pocket and pull the bench apart. the last stretch is the wrong order. i put the head in the dust and watch the bench shift again. maybe the screw is the wrong way."}]
